      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Spina bifida is a neural tube defect - a type of birth defect of the brain, <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spine, or spinal</span></span> cord. It happens if the <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> <span class="qt1">column</span> of the fetus doesn't close completely during the first month of pregnancy. This can damage the nerves and <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> cord. Screening tests during pregnancy can check for spina bifida. Sometimes it is discovered only after the baby is born.</p><p>The symptoms of spina bifida vary from person to person. Most people with spina bifida are of normal intelligence. Some people need assistive devices such as braces, crutches, or wheelchairs. They may have learning difficulties, urinary and bowel problems, or hydrocephalus, a buildup of fluid in the brain.</p><p>The exact cause of spina bifida is unknown. It seems to run in families. Taking folic acid can reduce the risk of having a baby with spina bifida. It's in most multivitamins. Women who could become pregnant should take it daily.</p><p>NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke</p></content>

      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Your backbone, or <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spine</span></span>, is made up of 26 bone discs called vertebrae. The vertebrae protect your <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> cord and allow you to stand and bend.  A number of problems can change the structure of the <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spine</span></span> or damage the vertebrae and surrounding tissue. They include:</p><ul><li>Infections</li><li>Injuries</li><li>Tumors</li><li>Conditions, such as ankylosing spondylitis and scoliosis</li><li>Bone changes that come with age, such as <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> stenosis and herniated disks</li></ul><p><span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">Spinal</span></span> diseases often cause pain when bone changes put pressure on the <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> cord or nerves. They can also limit movement. Treatments differ by disease, but sometimes they include back braces and surgery.</p></content>

    <document rank="2" url="https://medlineplus.gov/neckinjuriesanddisorders.html">
      <content name="title">Neck Injuries and Disorders</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Cervical <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">Spine</span></span></content>
      <content name="altTitle">Whiplash</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Any part of your neck - muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, or nerves - can cause neck problems. Neck pain is very common. Pain may also come from your shoulder, jaw, head, or upper arms. </p><p>Muscle strain or tension often causes neck pain. The problem is usually overuse, such as from sitting at a computer for too long.  Sometimes you can strain your neck muscles from sleeping in an awkward position or overdoing it during exercise. Falls or accidents, including car accidents, are another common cause of neck pain.  Whiplash, a soft tissue injury to the neck, is also called neck sprain or strain.</p><p>Treatment depends on the cause, but may include applying ice, taking pain relievers, getting physical therapy or wearing a cervical collar. You rarely need surgery.</p></content>

    <document rank="3" url="https://medlineplus.gov/neuraltubedefects.html">
      <content name="title">Neural Tube Defects</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Anencephaly</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Neural tube defects are birth defects of the brain, <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spine, or spinal</span></span> cord. They happen in the first month of pregnancy, often before a woman even knows that she is pregnant. The two most common neural tube defects are spina bifida and anencephaly. In spina bifida, the fetal <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> <span class="qt1">column</span> doesn't close completely. There is usually nerve damage that causes at least some paralysis of the legs. In anencephaly, most of the brain and skull do not develop. Babies with anencephaly are usually either stillborn or die shortly after birth. Another type of defect, Chiari malformation, causes the brain tissue to extend into the <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spinal</span></span> canal.</p><p>The exact causes of neural tube defects aren't known. You're at greater risk of having an infant with a neural tube defect if you:</p><ul><li>Have obesity</li><li>Have poorly controlled diabetes</li><li>Take certain antiseizure medicines</li></ul><p>Getting enough folic acid, a type of B vitamin, before and during pregnancy prevents most neural tube defects.</p><p>Neural tube defects are usually diagnosed before the infant is born, through lab or imaging tests. There is no cure for neural tube defects. The nerve damage and loss of function that are present at birth are usually permanent. However, a variety of treatments can sometimes prevent further damage and help with complications.</p><p>NIH: National Institute of Child Health and Human Development</p></content>

    <document rank="4" url="https://medlineplus.gov/herniateddisk.html">
      <content name="title">Herniated Disk</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Ruptured Disk</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Slipped Disk</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Bulging disk</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Compressed disk</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Herniated intervertebral disk</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Herniated nucleus pulposus</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Prolapsed disk</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Your backbone, or <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">spine</span></span>, is made up of 26 bones called vertebrae. In between them are soft disks filled with a jelly-like substance. These disks cushion the vertebrae and keep them in place. As you age, the disks break down or degenerate. As they do, they lose their cushioning ability. This can lead to pain if the back is stressed.</p><p>A herniated disk is a disk that ruptures. This allows the jelly-like center of the disk to leak, irritating the nearby nerves. This can cause sciatica or back pain.</p><p>Your doctor will diagnose a herniated disk with a physical exam and, sometimes, imaging tests. With treatment, most people recover. Treatments include rest, pain and anti-inflammatory medicines, physical therapy, and sometimes surgery.</p><p>NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases</p></content>
